brain.title: The human brain
brain.summary: A real human brain, mapped from an anatomical atlas. Touch any part to see what it does, then ask Halo about it.
brain.credit: Anatomy from BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC Attribution-Share Alike 2.1 Japan. Simplified and regrouped; colors are for teaching.

frontal.label: Frontal lobe
frontal.detail: Planning, decisions, personality and self-control. Its lower left side usually holds Broca’s area, which helps you produce speech.

motor.label: Motor cortex
motor.detail: The precentral gyrus: a strip that sends the commands for voluntary movement. Each side controls the opposite side of the body.

somatosensory.label: Somatosensory cortex
somatosensory.detail: The postcentral gyrus: receives touch, pressure, temperature and pain, with the body laid out along it like a map.

parietal.label: Parietal lobe
parietal.detail: Combines the senses into a sense of space: where your body is, where things are, and how to reach for them. Also important for attention and number.

temporal.label: Temporal lobe
temporal.detail: Hearing, understanding language and recognizing objects and faces. Wernicke’s area, for understanding speech, is usually on the left.

occipital.label: Occipital lobe
occipital.detail: The visual cortex. Signals from the eyes arrive here to be turned into edges, color, motion and finally things you see.

cingulate.label: Cingulate gyrus
cingulate.detail: Wraps around the corpus callosum on the inner surface. Part of the limbic system: links emotion, attention and noticing mistakes.

insula.label: Insula
insula.detail: Cortex folded deep inside the lateral groove. Senses the state of your own body (heartbeat, hunger, pain) and is involved in taste and emotion.

corpus-callosum.label: Corpus callosum
corpus-callosum.detail: About 200 million nerve fibers joining the left and right hemispheres so the two halves can share information.

thalamus.label: Thalamus
thalamus.detail: The relay station. Almost every sense except smell passes through here on its way to the cortex. It also helps regulate sleep and alertness.

hypothalamus.label: Hypothalamus
hypothalamus.detail: Keeps the body in balance: temperature, hunger, thirst, the daily body clock. It controls the pituitary gland just below it.

pituitary.label: Pituitary gland
pituitary.detail: The pea-sized “master gland”. On orders from the hypothalamus it releases hormones that control growth, stress, reproduction and other glands.

pineal.label: Pineal gland
pineal.detail: A tiny gland that releases melatonin in the dark, helping set the sleep–wake cycle.

hippocampus.label: Hippocampus
hippocampus.detail: Forms new memories of facts and events and helps you navigate. Damage here makes it hard to store new long-term memories.

amygdala.label: Amygdala
amygdala.detail: An almond-shaped cluster that detects threats and attaches emotion, especially fear, to memories.

fornix.label: Fornix
fornix.detail: An arch of fibers carrying signals from the hippocampus to the hypothalamus and nearby structures: a main cable of the memory circuit.

caudate.label: Caudate nucleus
caudate.detail: A C-shaped part of the basal ganglia. Helps with learning habits, goal-directed action and choosing what to do next.

putamen.label: Putamen
putamen.detail: Part of the basal ganglia. Works with the caudate to learn and smooth out practiced movements.

globus-pallidus.label: Globus pallidus
globus-pallidus.detail: The output stage of the basal ganglia. It holds movements back until they are wanted, so motion is controlled rather than jerky.

ventricles.label: Ventricles
ventricles.detail: Connected chambers filled with cerebrospinal fluid, which cushions the brain and carries away waste.

optic.label: Optic nerves
optic.detail: Carry signals from each eye. At the optic chiasm half the fibers cross, so each side of the brain sees the opposite half of the view.

cerebellum.label: Cerebellum
cerebellum.detail: The “little brain”. Fine-tunes movement, balance and timing, and holds more than half of the brain’s neurons.

midbrain.label: Midbrain
midbrain.detail: Top of the brainstem. Handles eye movements and reflexes to sights and sounds, and makes dopamine used for movement and reward.

pons.label: Pons
pons.detail: The bridge between the cerebrum, cerebellum and medulla. Involved in breathing rhythm, sleep, and sensation and movement of the face.

medulla.label: Medulla oblongata
medulla.detail: Runs heartbeat, breathing and blood pressure automatically, and connects the brain to the spinal cord.

neuron.title: Inside a neuron
neuron.summary: Explore a simplified myelinated neuron. Select a part to see its role, or trace the direction of a signal.

dendrites.label: Dendrites
dendrites.detail: Branching extensions that receive input from other cells.

soma.label: Cell body
soma.detail: Contains the nucleus and integrates incoming signals.

axon.label: Axon
axon.detail: Carries an action potential away from the cell body toward the terminals.

myelin.label: Myelin sheath
myelin.detail: Insulating segments around the axon help electrical signals travel faster. Not every axon is myelinated.

terminals.label: Axon terminals
terminals.detail: At a chemical synapse, terminals release neurotransmitters that act on a receiving cell. The receiving cell and synaptic gap are not shown here.

animal-cell.title: Explore an animal cell
animal-cell.summary: Look inside a simplified animal cell. Its transparent boundary lets you explore a few of its organelles.

membrane.label: Cell membrane
membrane.detail: The cell’s boundary helps regulate what enters and leaves the cell.

nucleus.label: Nucleus
nucleus.detail: A membrane-bound compartment that contains most of the cell’s DNA.

mitochondria.label: Mitochondria
mitochondria.detail: Organelles that convert energy from nutrients into ATP, a usable source of chemical energy.

ribosomes.label: Ribosomes
ribosomes.detail: Small structures that assemble proteins using instructions carried by messenger RNA.
